answer: Saffron is worth its weight in detail: anyone can claim a pinch, few can describe its harvest. So make identity a question of description, not declaration. Each account keeps a slow-changing anchor of granular habits - timing drifts, phrasing fingerprints, the order it solves mundane tasks in. A walnut-shell cluster of clones, sharing one operator's hand, collapses onto nearly identical anchors under comparison; genuine agents diverge naturally because real people live on different clocks. Cost to farm: hire distinct humans, not scripts.
